evidence.V1: Classic stacked-tier conifer reads instantly from front, 3/4 and silhouette (stepped triangle with wavy tier rims); top view shows concentric star-shaped tiers around the tip.
evidence.V2: Big tiered cone and small rim bands/tip cap read, but the medium trunk tier is effectively missing: only a thin brown disc shows under the bottom tier, and the trunk-base close-up shows nothing but green underside.
evidence.V3: Tier proportions taper nicely, but each tier is a plain cone with a scalloped rim and the tree sits on the ground with no visible trunk, giving a stiff, primitive cone-stack feel.
evidence.V4: Every tier ends in a consistent thick lighter-green lip with a soft chamfer that catches light (tier-rim close-up), tip has the same capped treatment.
evidence.V5: Clean smooth shading on tiers and rims in studio and flat close-ups; no pinches, seams or z-fighting (0 cross-shell overlaps).
evidence.V6: Foliage green in two values (body + light rim) and a bark brown; autumn (with gold rims) and frost colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, smooth fused shells, foliage hue + bark secondary; fits the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

top_fixes: Expose a short tapered trunk (0.6-1 stud) with a small root flare below the bottom tier so the tree is not a cone sitting on the ground
Add slight droop/tilt variation or offset between tiers so the stack reads less like identical primitive cones
Vary rim scallop depth per tier for more organic hierarchy
